title: Touch screen, price hike to cheapest Sony e-reader
summary: Sony is adding a touch-screen to its cheapest e-reader, the Reader Pocket Edition, and increasing its price by $29, betting that consumers will pay more for the new feature. The company is also upgrading its larger-screen Reader models, the Daily Edition and the Touch Edition, with the same touch-screen technology and increased memory. Despite the price hikes, some models will still be cheaper than their original prices last year, while competitor Borders Group Inc. cut prices on two of its e-book readers.

title: Sonos ZonePlayer S5 (aka PLAY:5) Review: Look Ma. No Wires. - Dennis Burger
summary: This review details the Sonos ZonePlayer S5 (later renamed PLAY:5), highlighting its ease of setup, surprisingly good sound quality for its size, and extensive integration with various streaming music services. The author praises its portability and intuitive user interface while noting minor drawbacks like the need for additional Sonos hardware for full wireless functionality and a slight hiccup in syncing iTunes with the system. Ultimately, the S5 is presented as a smart, compact, and hard-to-resist audio device for multiroom sound.

title: Shifting Online, Netflix Faces New Competition (Published 2010)
summary: Netflix is shifting its focus from DVD rentals to online streaming, facing new competition from major tech companies like Apple, Amazon, and Google, as well as cable providers. The company's future success depends on its ability to negotiate content rights with Hollywood studios for its streaming service, which currently has a limited selection compared to its DVD catalog. Netflix is experimenting with streaming-only subscriptions, starting in Canada, and analysts anticipate a decline in its DVD business as it transitions to online content.

title: Apple Outpaces Google in Media Attention – Both Get Positive Play
summary: A Pew Research Center report from June 2009 through June 2010 indicates that Apple Inc. received more mainstream media coverage than any other technology company, with 15% of tech stories focusing on Apple compared to 11% for Google Inc. Both companies largely received positive press, with Apple's coverage highlighting product innovation and a loyal fan base, while Google's focused on its navigational utility but also touched on concerns about its data power. Microsoft, Twitter, and Facebook also received attention, with Microsoft significantly trailing its peers.

title: Maker of BlackBerry introduces PlayBook tablet
summary: Research In Motion (R.I.M.), the maker of BlackBerry, introduced its first tablet computer, the BlackBerry PlayBook, aimed primarily at business users. R.I.M. hopes to distinguish the PlayBook from Apple's iPad by offering features requested by corporate IT departments, including compatibility with corporate servers and the ability to display Flash content. While the company revealed some features, details on pricing and a specific release date were left vague, though it's expected early next year.
